prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
ai_overview_text:
Choose Airbnb for urban areas, diverse properties (like single rooms or unique stays), and shorter trips; choose Vrbo for whole-home vacation rentals, beach/ski resorts, and larger family groups; and choose Booking.com if you are traveling in Europe or prefer a hotel-like booking experience. Reddit·r/airbnb_hosts +3
Platform Comparison
FeatureAirbnbVrboBooking.comBest ForCity stays, unique rentals, solo/couplesFamilies, groups, whole-home rentals (3+ bedrooms)Europe, apartments competing with hotels, flexible staysProperty TypesApartments, single rooms, treehouses, villasEntire homes, cabins, beach houses, villasEntire apartments, homes, and traditional hotelsPricing / FeesGuest fees run roughly 5% to 15%Booking fees run roughly 6% to 12% (defaults to upfront total pricing)Varies; "free cancellation" options can have higher nightly rates
Check Overall Ratings & Badges: Look for high star averages (4.9+ on Airbnb, or "Premier Host" status on Vrbo indicating low cancellations and fast response rates). Rentals United
Read Detailed Reviews: Do not rely on star counts alone. Read recent guest comments to see how the host handles problems, noise, or check-in issues. Unsalted Vacations +1
Inspect Photo Quality: Good hosts show real, clear photos of every room, storage areas, and the building exterior rather than generic stock images of the neighborhood. Facebook·Wolters World
Test Communication: Message the host with a quick question before booking. A great host responds quickly, clearly, and helpfully. Unsalted Vacations
Avoid Brand-New Listings: Be cautious of profiles with zero reviews or only one or two generic reviews unless you are willing to risk unverified service. Facebook·Wolters World
